title: fix(live-e2e): the backend cold install writes overrides.vitest so npm 10 can install the published graph (objectui#12649)
body:
Fixes #12649

Clause-②: no

The `Live E2E (informational)` lane's backend now installs cold on the runner's npm. `e2e/live/ci/start-backend.sh` writes one root `overrides` entry, `vitest: ~4.0.0`, into the rewritten showcase manifest. The same value is the third component of the fixture stamp, so a fixture prepared under another install recipe is rebuilt, not reused. The CI/CD guide's paragraph that said "no transitive dependency is overridden" now names this one and says what the fixture cache still cannot see.

## Reproduction

- **Runner npm**, read from the failing job's `actions/setup-node` step (job 116927385035): Node 22.23.3, npm 10.9.9.
- Every local run below ran the real script end to end, under npm 10.9.9 or 11.21.0 fetched into a temp prefix, with a fresh npm cache and a fresh `LIVE_BACKEND_DIR`.
- **Baseline**, the `origin/main` script at `f78efdd1e` under npm 10.9.9: exit 1 with `npm error Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')`. The stack is in `#loadPeerSet` under `idealTree:node_modules/@objectstack/cli`. That is the CI failure, reproduced on the runner's npm.
- **Why it crashes:** the installed graph reaches `vitest` only as an optional peer, from `better-auth@1.7.3` (nested under `@objectstack/plugin-auth`) and from `@objectstack/metadata-core@18.0.0-next.2`. That was read by scanning the installed tree. Upstream today, `npm view vitest dist-tags` gives `V4: 4.1.12`, and the 4.x line of `@vitest/browser-webdriverio` ends at `4.1.11`.

## Remedy chosen, and the alternatives' readings

| route | npm | install | boot: sign-in · `/api/v1/health` · `/api/v1/ready` | allowlist | installed tree |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **(a) `overrides.vitest: ~4.0.0` (chosen)** | 10.9.9 | exit 0, 528 packages | ready · 200 · 200 | 5 passed | same as (b); no vitest installed |
| (b) npm 11, no override | 11.21.0 | exit 0, 528 packages | ready · 200 · 200 | 5 passed | the reference |
| (c) `--legacy-peer-deps` | 10.9.9 | exit 0, 506 packages | ready · 200 · 200 | 5 passed | differs from (b) |

- **Why (a).** It is the simplest correct route. It is objectstack's documented remedy for this crash: the troubleshooting entry "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut') from npm install", objectstack `7a6ba03109`. objectstack's scaffolds emit the same override (objectstack-ai/objectstack#23850).
- **(a) installs the tree (b) installs.** The two lockfiles' `packages` maps were compared path for path and version for version: 554 entries each, and no difference beyond npm 10 and npm 11 writing different `optional`/`peer` flags. So the lane still tests the published pair.
- **(b)** is equally correct, but it adds a runtime npm download to the script and installs no different tree.
- **(c)** installs a tree nobody ships. It drops `@objectstack/plugin-auth`'s `better-sqlite3@12.11.1` peer with its 21-package build subtree, and hoists `better-auth` to the root. The claim allowed it only as the last resort.

## Boot and allowlist proof: what was measured, and what was not

- **(a), cold, through the changed script:** the install exits 0. The script's own readiness probe, the seeded admin's sign-in, answered. `GET /api/v1/health` gave 200 (`status: ok`, `version: 18.0.0-next.2`), and `GET /api/v1/ready` gave 200 (`status: ready`).
- **Allowlist:** the console was built with `VITE_BASE_PATH=/`, as in the workflow's `Build console` step, and served by `vite preview` with `DEV_PROXY_TARGET` at the backend. The four specs `test:e2e:live:ci` names ran: `5 passed`.
- **Two container-only deviations in that run:** the browser was the preinstalled Chromium, through the launch `executablePath`, and video recording was off, because this container has no ffmpeg for this Playwright revision. Both came from a scratch config that spread `playwright.live.config.ts` and changed nothing else. It was deleted afterwards and is not in this diff.
- **The stamp, both directions:**
  - Rerunning the changed script on its own prepared fixture printed `prepare: pins unchanged (… 18.0.0-next.2 vitest@~4.0.0), reusing`, in 13 s with no install.
  - Running it on a fixture the `origin/main` script had prepared printed `prepare: showcase@…` and installed cold again: exit 0, 528 packages. That fixture's stamp has no third component, which is what a restored cache would carry.
- **NOT MEASURED here:** the GitHub runner itself (only its Node and npm versions were reproduced), and the nightly schedule path.

## Is this PR's own Live E2E run cold?

- The fixture cache key is `live-backend-` plus the runner OS plus `hashFiles('e2e/live/ci/backend.env')`. This PR does not touch `backend.env`, so the key stays `3e640c78135ae9fa…`.
  - That hash was recomputed locally as the sha256 of the file's sha256. It matches the key the failing job printed, which is the positive control.
- No cache under that key is readable by this PR. A pull request run reads its own caches and `main`'s, and `main`'s are written only by the nightly schedule and manual dispatch. The workflow's run list since 11:00Z on 2026-10-16 shows only `pull_request` runs, so nothing on `main` has saved a fixture since `f62b6ff` moved `backend.env`.
- Even on a hit, the stamp's new third component rejects any fixture prepared without it, so the script cold-installs.
- This body is written once. The reading of the run itself, from its `Start ObjectStack backend (published packages)` step, goes in the os-dev report on #12649.

## What the cache still hides

- The key hashes `backend.env` alone. So a cold install that breaks because the registry moved under unchanged pins stays hidden until `OBJECTSTACK_VERSION` moves. That is how this one broke: the card's `18.0.0-next.1` control fails the same way.
- Closing that needs a periodic cold run or a committed backend lockfile. The first is a workflow edit, which is governed and outside this claim, so it is named here and in the report, not done. The docs page now states the limit.

## Removal condition

- **Written at the override:** remove `VITEST_OVERRIDE`, the `overrides` line in `prepare()`, and the stamp's third component once the published `@objectstack/cli` at `OBJECTSTACK_VERSION` installs on npm 10 with no override.
- That is not yet true. objectstack's metadata-core change (objectstack-ai/objectstack#23834) is not in a published `next`, and `better-auth`'s optional vitest peer reaches the crash on its own.
- **The comment gives the re-measure recipe, and warns of a trap measured here.** Delete the override in a prepared dir and run `npm install` again, and npm answers `up to date` with exit 0, because it installs from the lockfile. That rerun proves nothing; only a fresh dir does.

## Gates (local, at `eed841f45`)

- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test e2e/live/ci/start-backend.sh content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md`: exit 0, `NOT GOVERNED`.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0, no changeset owed. The two files are neither published source nor a release-covered manifest.
- These all exit 0: `check-bash32-floor`, `check-doc-links`, `check-control-bytes`, `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` (0 new), `check-doc-fence-languages` and `check-shell-escape-residue`. `bash -n` on the script is clean.
- `check-doc-json-fences` first refused with exit 2, a prerequisite: `@object-ui/types` was not built. After the build it exits 0.
- **Tests:** `pnpm exec vitest run` over the 17 test files that name `ci-cd-pipeline.md` or `start-backend.sh` (found with `git grep -l`): 17 files and 737 tests passed.
- Everything else is CI's, read from this PR's check-runs.

## Acceptance notes

- **`stop-backend.sh` does not stop the backend. This is pre-existing and not touched here.**
  - `start()` records `$!` of a backgrounded `cd … && nohup … objectstack dev` list. That is the forked subshell, not the server.
  - Measured with the `origin/main` scripts: the pid file held 30766, and the server was 30767, its child. `stop-backend.sh` printed `stopped pid 30766` and exited 0, while `/api/v1/health` on the port still answered 200. The server was reparented to pid 1.
  - CI never calls it (ephemeral runner), so the lane is unaffected. The local recipe it exists for leaks the server and the port. It goes to the seat as a finding.
- **The cache's remaining blind spot** is above.
